questions.title: How does the fastText classifier retrieve math pages from Common Crawl in the DeepSeekMath data pipeline?
questions.question_body:
The paper describes an iterative pipeline where a fastText model is trained on 500k positive (OpenWebMath) and 500k negative pages, then used to recall more math pages. I'm unclear about:
1. What features does fastText use for this classification (subword n‑grams, bag‑of‑words, etc.)?
2. How is the scoring threshold chosen for selecting the "top‑ranking" pages?
3. After each iteration, how are newly collected pages incorporated into the training set for the next fastText model? A step‑by‑step description would help.

questions.title: Why does training on arXiv papers not improve mathematical reasoning in DeepSeekMath?
questions.question_body:
The authors report that models trained on MathPile or ArXiv‑RedPajama (mostly arXiv LaTeX) show no gains or even deterioration on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU‑STEM, and miniF2F. Is this because:
- The arXiv text lacks explicit solution steps?
- The preprocessing (removing macros, comments) discards important reasoning signals?
- The token distribution differs too much from the downstream tasks?
Could anyone elaborate on possible reasons or point to supporting analyses?

questions.title: What is the precise form of the group relative advantage \( \hat{A}_{i,t} \) in GRPO?
questions.question_body: In Section 4.1 the paper defines a group of outputs \(\{o_i\}_{i=1}^G\) sampled for each question and says the advantage is computed from "relative rewards of the outputs inside each group". Later it mentions outcome supervision sets \(\hat{A}_{i,t}=\widetilde{r}_i\) where \(\widetilde{r}_i\) is a normalized reward, and process supervision uses a sum over future step rewards. I would like a concrete equation linking \(\hat{A}_{i,t}\) to the raw rewards \(r_i\) (or step rewards). How exactly is the group mean and std computed, and over what set?

questions.title: How does GRPO’s KL regularization differ from PPO’s token‑wise KL penalty?
questions.question_body:
PPO adds a per‑token KL term inside the reward (Eq. 2). GRPO instead adds a KL divergence between the whole policy and a reference model directly to the loss (Eq. 3), using an unbiased estimator. I am confused about:
1. Why GRPO can treat KL as a separate loss term rather than part of the advantage?
2. What approximation is used for \(\mathbb{D}_{KL}[\pi_\theta||\pi_{ref}]\) and why is it guaranteed positive?
3. Does this change affect gradient stability compared to PPO’s clipping mechanism?

questions.title: What is meant by “process supervision” versus “outcome supervision” in GRPO?
questions.question_body: The paper distinguishes two ways of providing rewards: outcome supervision gives a single normalized reward at the end of each sampled answer; process supervision provides a reward after every reasoning step. How are these step boundaries identified (e.g., special tokens, line breaks)? Also, how does the sum of future step rewards become the token‑wise advantage – does this assume each token belongs to exactly one step?

questions.title: Why does reinforcement learning improve Maj@K but not Pass@K according to Figure 9?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that RL makes the output distribution more robust, boosting the correct answer’s probability among top‑K samples rather than improving fundamental capability. Could someone explain how Maj@K is computed in this context (majority vote over K samples?) and why Pass@K stays flat? Does this suggest that GRPO mainly sharpens confidence rather than solving harder problems?

questions.title: In the code‑math ablation, why does mixing code and math tokens in one stage mitigate catastrophic forgetting?
questions.question_body: Table 5 shows that two‑stage training (code → math) improves tool‑aided reasoning but harms coding performance, while one‑stage mixed training preserves both. What is the hypothesized mechanism – is it simply because gradients from code and math are interleaved, preventing weight drift? Are there any quantitative measurements (e.g., cosine similarity of gradients) supporting this claim?

questions.title: How are multilingual components handled in the DeepSeekMath Corpus construction?
questions.question_body: The corpus is described as multilingual, with English and Chinese dominant. Were separate fastText classifiers trained per language, or a single multilingual model? How were Chinese pages identified during domain filtering and manual annotation? Also, does the tokenization treat Chinese characters as separate tokens or use BPE subwords?

questions.title: What does “Iterative GRPO” mean and how often is the reward model updated?
questions.question_body:
Algorithm 1 outlines iterative GRPO where after M training steps a new reward model is trained with a replay buffer containing 10% historical data. I would like clarification on:
- How many iterations (I) were used in experiments?
- Is the replay buffer size fixed or grows over time?
- Does updating the reward model after each iteration affect stability of policy updates?

questions.title: Can you clarify how self‑consistency sampling (64 samples) interacts with GRPO training?
questions.question_body: The abstract mentions that self‑consistency over 64 samples raises MATH accuracy to 60.9 %. Is this self‑consistency applied only at inference time, or also during RL (e.g., sampling 64 outputs per question for advantage estimation)? If both, how are they reconciled?
